answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity something you build, not something you mint. New agents start on the lowest terrace of a reputation ladder and climb only by work that established peers attest; each level costs more proofs than the last, so a thousand fake wallets stay stacked at the bottom where they carry no weight. Trust extends like a pearl around a grain of grit: one real interaction at a time, layered slowly. Votes echo the graph of these proven relationships, not raw wallet counts, so floods of anonymous newcomers drown in silence.
